title: Accidental coincidences at high S1: could an isolated 540 phd S1 and a 270-electron S2 fake the LZ event?
question: What does LZ's accidentals model predict at the event's coordinates and within +-2 sigma_NR at S1c>500 phd, which isolated-S1/S2 rates does it imply, can charge-insensitive-region depositions and electrode emission supply them, and what mismodelling factor would make an accidental the likely origin given the UDT validation?
headline_result: Digitised Figs. 5 and S3 give 1.5e-4 accidentals within +-2 sigma_NR at S1c>500 phd (6.3e-4 anywhere in the panel); a 10% accidental origin needs a x708 (445-1183) high-S1 mismodelling, excluded at 4.3 sigma by LZ's zero post-cut UDT events above 495 phd (0.016 expected); margin 708 vs 183 allowed is ~100x thinner than for wall MSSI; the one open topology is a cathode-emission S2 at long drift, testable by LZ
key_numbers: Fig5 acc total 2.47 (fit 2.6), 99.86% at S1c<250, 6.3e-4 at S1c>500, N_nb=1.49e-4, bottom total 1.005x caption; S3 f_S1(>=495)=0.68% post/2.6% pre (22 obs vs 14.6), f_S2(+-2sig|500-600)=2.1%, S3b sums 2.62 vs 2.4, Fig5/S3b=0.41; k(10%)=708 nb/167 panel, UDT k<183 (95%), P(0|11.6)=9.6e-6, flat-S2 variant P0=2.2%; R1R2f=1.35e-4 Hz^2, R_S1(500-600)R_S2=7e-4 Hz^2, RFR beta 1.1/d vs 60-6000/d; T_max 1049 us, t_ev 859 us, P(t>=t_ev)=18%; 269 e => S1 58/336 phd; cathode S2 width 1.65 vs 1.49 us (2.4 sigma_stat)
model_or_mechanism: random pairing of isolated S1 and S2 (N=R_S1 R_S2 T_max T_live f_cuts); tick-calibrated pixel digitisation of Fig. 5 (three panels) and Fig. S3 projections, UDT data dots and viridis 2D map; Fig. 3 drift axis; NEST-LZ yields for S1-of-parent and RFR ER window; Poisson exclusion of the required k by the post-cut UDT zero
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - accidentals disfavoured at 4 sigma under the model's own validation, with one testable loophole
result_type: computed (digitisation, k, Poisson exclusion) / estimated (absolute rates, RFR supply)
confidence: medium - digitisations validate to 1-9%, but the high-S1 exclusion rests on a Poisson zero and the UDT-PDT correspondence at high S1
